source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.heading: Verse 1
entries.text: Ps 149:1-9 . This Psalm sustains a close connection with the foregoing. The chosen people are exhorted to praise God, in view of past favors, and also future victories over enemies, of which they are impliedly assured.
2. God had signalized His relation as a sovereign, in restoring them to their land.

entries.heading: 3. in the dance
entries.text: 3. in the dance -- ( Ps 30:11 ). The dance is connected with other terms, expressive of the great joy of the occasion. The word may be rendered "lute," to which the other instruments are joined. sing praises --or, sing and play.

entries.heading: 4. taketh pleasure
entries.text: 4. taketh pleasure --literally, "accepts," alluding to acceptance of propitiatory offerings (compare Ps 147:11 ). beautify, &c.--adorn the humble with faith, hope, joy, and peace.

entries.heading: 5. in glory
entries.text: 5. in glory --the honorable condition to which they are raised. upon their beds --once a place of mourning ( Ps 6:6 ).

entries.heading: 6. high praises
entries.text: 6. high praises --or, "deeds." They shall go forth as religious warriors, as once religious laborers ( Ne 4:17 ).
7. The destruction of the incorrigibly wicked attends the propagation of God's truth, so that the military successes of the Jews, after the captivity, typified the triumphs of the Gospel.

entries.heading: 9. the judgment written
entries.text: 9. the judgment written --either in God's decrees, or perhaps as in De 32:41-43 . this honour --that is, to be thus employed, will be an honorable service, to be assigned his saints --or, godly ones ( Ps 16:3 ).
